In a row there are 23 numbers such that the sum of any two adjacent numbers is 17. The second number is 6. What is the last number?
Find the missing number: 3, 8, ?, 15, 17, 18

There are 19 numbers in a row such that the sum of any two adjacent numbers is 13. The second number 
is 5. What is the last number?
Alikhan wrote numbers on the board according to a certain rule: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. What number will be next?
In the school auditorium, each subsequent row has 2 more seats than the previous one. There are 20 seats in the last row and 6 in the first. How many rows are there in the auditorium?

Aset has a robot that can turn numbers into other numbers. It takes a number and then says another number. Look at the table: 

What number will the robot say if it receives the number 6?
Ainur and Kymbat picked 38 plums together. When they ate the plums equally, Ainur had 3  plums left, and Kymbat had 11 plums left.  How many  plums did Ainur pick?
Arman and Miras collected 47 nuts together. After they ate the same amount of nuts, Arman had 10 nuts left, and Miras had 19. How many nuts did Armand collect?

Sultan wanted to buy some apples in the store. He had 100 tenge. The price of 1 apple 
is 6 tenge. He bought as many apples as he could. How many tenge does Sultan have 
left after buying the apples?

Grandparents are watering raspberry bushes in their garden. First, the grandmother watered 7 bushes. Then grandfather watered 9 bushes. As a result, 5 bushes were watered twice, and 2
bushes were left without water. How many raspberry bushes are there in the garden?
The confectioner baked 7 banana cakes and 5 chocolate cakes. She baked 10 cakes in total. How many cakes are both banana and chocolate?

There are 30 children in the kindergarten. 12 of them like drawing, and 18 like building with blocks. Half of those who like building also like drawing. How many children do not like either drawing or building?

There are three teachers working in the kindergarten: Sarah, Alua and Inkar. Exactly two of them work 
every day from Monday to Friday. Sarah works three days, and Alua four. How many days does Inkar 
work? Explain the answer

Grandparents are watering raspberry bushes in their garden. First, grandmother watered 13 
bushes. Then grandfather watered 17 bushes. As a result, 7 bushes were watered twice, and 6  bushes were left without watering.  How many raspberry bushes are there in the garden?

There are 10 members in a mathematics club. They perform three activities: giving lessons, creating exams, and solving problems. Each member participates in exactly two activities from the list. 
- Mathematicians with numbers 10, 4, 5, 7, 6, 9, 1 gave lessons. 
- Mathematicians with numbers 2, 4, 9, 7, 10, 8, 3 created exams. 
Find how many mathematicians were involved in solving problems.

Three dice are glued together, as shown in the figure. It turned out that the sum of the points on the visible faces (top and sides) is 45. What is the sum of the points on the invisible faces?
(A dice is a cube with dots from 1 to 6 on its sides)
Which of the figures A–E cannot be assembled from the two shown pieces?

On a dice, the total number of points on any two opposite faces is 7. Jazira glued a column of 3 such dices together and counted the total number of points on all outer faces. What's the biggest number she could get?
How many cubes are shown in the picture?
Different parts were cut from the cubes. Find the missing details:
Draw how this picture looks from above.
If this picture is made into a cube, what is the number of dots that will be on top, if at bottom there are 3 dots?

The kitten can jump to any adjacent cell by side to it and has enough strength for only three 
jumps. How many cells can a mouse safely sit in?

The figure below is a net of a cube and every face is labeled with a letter or a digit. If the net 
is made into a cube by folding, which letter or digit is on the face opposite to the face with the 
letter "F"?

How many small cubes will be needed to complete the shape from the figure below to 
a solid 3 × 3 × 3 cube?

Olzhas had a rectangular bar of chocolate, divided into small squares. He ate several squares, and a piece remained on the plate, which can be seen in the figure. Calculate the minimum number of squares of chocolate Olzhas ate to leave such a piece.
Two sausages were eaten by two cats in two minutes. How many sausages will 4 cats eat in 4 minutes?

Several ducks are walking in the yard. These ducks have 9 more feet than noses. How many ducks are 
there in the yard?
One apple and two pears together weigh as much as twelve lemons. Two pears together weigh as much as three apples. How many lemons weigh as much as one apple?

topic: Odd one out / visual pattern recognition
prob: Find in each row the letter that is significantly different from the other letters in its row, and write them down in order. What word do you get?

topic: Arithmetic word problem – finding the whole or part
prob: Grandma has 7 large empty boxes and 5 small ones. Her grandson put small boxes inside large ones. How many empty large boxes are left, if he put 2 small boxes into each of 2 large boxes?
The first ant crawled along the whole of line A, and the second ant along the whole of line B (both lines are shown in the picture). The second ant crawled 10 metres. How far did the first ant crawl?

Egor cut three three-cell L-shaped pieces (trominoes) out of the figure in the picture along the grid lines, and cut the rest into 2x2 squares with nothing left over. How many 2x2 squares did he get? (The three-cell corner piece may be rotated.)
Geese and goats are walking in a meadow. Altogether they have 16 legs, and there are two more geese than goats. How many geese are in the meadow?

Petya knows how many different colours of socks are in his chest of drawers. He needs to take out a pair of the same colour, but the room is dark. Clever Petya thought about it and realised that he would have to take out at least 7 socks to be guaranteed a pair of socks of the same colour. How many colours are Petya's socks?

7 hamsters and 3 guinea pigs weigh 16 pounds, and 3 hamsters weigh the same as one guinea pig. How many pounds does one guinea pig weigh? (All hamsters weigh the same, and all guinea pigs weigh the same.)
Petya has 6 more pies than Roma. If Petya gives Roma as many pies as Roma already has, they will have an equal number of pies. How many pies did Petya have?

Four gnomes brought Snow White shoes, earrings, a scarf and gloves. She wants to put them all on one after another, and she wants to put the scarf on after the earrings (not necessarily immediately after the earrings). In how many ways can she put these items on?

There are 30 children in a class. Exactly 10 children did not watch "Smeshariki", exactly 6 children did not watch "Luntik", and exactly 4 children watched neither cartoon. How many children watched both cartoons?

topic: Arithmetic word problem – finding the whole or part
prob: Marina has 7 pens in her pencil case - blue and red ones. In the Russian lesson she took 4 pens out of the case: 3 blue and one red. In the maths lesson she took out 5 pens: 4 red and one blue. Mum bought Marina two more red pens and put them in the case. How many red pens does Marina have now?

Ellina wrote the digits from 1 to 6 on the faces of a cube so that the sum of the digits on opposite faces was 7. Ira rubbed out the digits 4, 5 and 6. Ellina wrote them again on the empty faces, but now each digit was written on a different face from the one it was on before. Now, on the face opposite the one with 4, there is the digit 2. Which digit is on the face opposite the one with 6?

Several natural numbers (not necessarily different) are written on the board, and their sum is 50. The sum of the three largest of them is 30, and the sum of the two smallest is 9. How many numbers are written on the board?

A group of children was taken on an excursion to a sweet factory. At the end, each child was allowed to take 3 sweets of different kinds. In total the children took away 2 "Arktika" sweets, 3 "Belochka", 4 "Wolf and Red Riding Hood", 6 "Grilyazh", 5 "Dzhigit" and 10 "Eralash". How many children took an "Eralash" but did not take a "Belochka"?

One day Tolya found himself in a large group of people. Four people were 2 years younger than him, seven people were 3 years older, and the remaining three people were 4 years older. All together (counting Tolya) they were 190 years old. How old is Tolya?

Masha has 36 balls. One digit is written on each of them: the digit 1 on nine balls, the digit 2 also on nine, the digit 3 on nine, and the digit 4 also on nine. Masha took 4 boxes and put the balls into them, 9 balls in each. The sum of the numbers written on the balls in the first box was 15, in the second 17, and in the third 22. Masha became curious about which numbers were written on the balls in the 4th box. She took out the first ball, looked at it and set it aside. Then the second, then the third. What number was on the 4th ball she took out?

8 children stood in a row, and there were more girls than boys. Each of them had a bag of sweets. Each child gave one sweet to everyone standing to the right of them. All the girls together ended up with 15 more sweets than they had before. How many boys were there?

Vova has a collection of different toy cars, and Dima has different toy soldiers. They can exchange one car for one soldier in 24 ways. One day Vova lost one car, and now they can make the exchange in 16 ways. How many cars did Vova have at the start?

There are 26 people in Kostya's class, and there are more boys than girls. In the summer Kostya went to the countryside for 5 days with some of his boy classmates. It was hot, and everyone managed to swim in the river. On the first day 10 people swam, on the second 9, on the third 7, on the fourth 2, and on the fifth just one person. Nobody swims more than once a day. Everyone except Kostya swam the same number of times, and Kostya swam fewer times than anyone. How many people went to the countryside (including Kostya)?

Vasya, Anya, Borya and Yana are standing along a straight road. Borya is 46 metres to the right of Anya, and Vasya is 23 metres to the right of Borya. Vasya is the furthest to the right. The sum of the distances from Yana to Anya, from Yana to Borya and from Yana to Vasya is 102 metres. What is the distance from Yana to Anya?
Petya built a large triangle out of small triangular cards, and the cat Pushok knocked several cards away with his tail. How many cards did Pushok knock away?

Mark's telephone number consists of seven different digits arranged in increasing order. Moreover, the fourth digit is equal to the product of the first three. What telephone number should be dialled to call Mark?
Today's date, 14.11.25, is beautiful because 14 + 11 = 25. Today is Friday. On what day of the week will the next date of the same beauty fall?

In the theatre "Molniya" Buratino has 40 spectator seats. The number of seats in one row of the stalls is equal to the number of rows in the stalls, and the number of seats in a box is equal to the number of boxes. It is known that there are more rows in the stalls than there are boxes. By how many more?

Lerochka wrote out all the three-digit numbers in which the sum of the first two digits equals the sum of the last two digits. How much time did she spend on this, if she takes 2 seconds to write one digit? Give the answer in seconds.

The Learned Cat can calculate in his head. If you tell him a number, the Cat will either multiply it by 2 or add 3 to it. After that he will either divide the result by 3 or subtract 4 from it, and tell you what he got at the end. Petya thought of a whole number and told it to the Cat four times, and each time the Cat gave a different number in reply: first 5, then 8, then 3. What number did the Cat give the fourth time?
Katya cut her ribbon into 20 equal pieces. If she had cut it into 17 equal pieces, then each piece would have been 6 cm longer. How long was Katya's ribbon? Give the answer in centimetres.

Four cuts were made in a square from edge to edge: two vertical and two horizontal. The square then fell apart into nine rectangles. The sum of their perimeters is 84 cm. What was the area of the original square?

A boat travels down the river from the village to the camp in 3 hours, and back in 2 hours. Tanya was travelling by boat from the village to the camp and dropped a small ball into the river at the mill; the ball floated to the village at the same moment as Tanya arrived at the camp. How many metres is the mill from the village, if the distance from the village to the camp along the river is 6000 metres?

In a 3x3x3 cube, a frog or a toad sits in each 1x1x1 small cube. Frogs always tell the truth, and toads always lie. Each of them said: "I have a toad for a neighbour!" What is the largest number of toads there could have been among them? (Neighbours share a common face.)

The digits of today's date (15.02.2026) are written on Christmas baubles. Hang the baubles on three Christmas trees so that the sums of the digits on each tree are the same. Show your answer on the picture.

Neznaika wrote words on the blackboard with chalks of different colours (red, green and blue), each word in its own colour. Tsvetik noticed that the green word is above the longest word, and the red word is to the left of the shortest word. What colour is the letter TS? (The words on the board are GOROD (town), LUNA (moon) and SOLNTSE (sun).)

Vanya, Sanya and Anya each have a tangerine. Sanya's and Vanya's tangerines have the same number of segments, and Anya's has several segments fewer. The boys each gave Anya 1 segment, and then everyone had an equal number of segments. How many fewer segments were there in Anya's tangerine?

Two snails are crawling along the sides of a square from neighbouring corners towards each other, as shown in the picture. When they met, it turned out that the first had crawled 8 metres and the second only 7 metres. What was the distance between the snails at the start?

Arriving on the Moon, Neznaika met unusual little folk who lie either only in the morning or only in the evening. In the evening five of them said to Neznaika: "You are my best friend", and seven others said: "Tomorrow I will buy you an ice cream." The next morning Neznaika asked each of them the question: "Did you lie to me yesterday evening?" How many answers of "yes" will he get?
There are 5 fewer snowflakes in the rectangle than in the square. How many snowflakes are in the grey part of the square?

Petya has two cards with two different digits on the different sides. He can make the numbers 13, 35 and 58 from them. What other numbers can be made using these two cards? List all the possibilities.

Pirates landed on an island at the point marked on the map. One of them remembers this route to the treasure, starting from that point: "EENSNEEESS". The letters in the route mean a shift by one point in the given direction; for example, E means one point to the east, that is, to the right. It turned out that the old pirate remembered one of the letters wrongly, so there is no treasure at the end point of the route. Mark all the points where the treasure could be. Show your answer on the picture. (On the compass in the picture: S = north, YU = south, V = east, Z = west.)

Kira said: "I only tell the truth." Borya said: "Kira is lying." Alisa objected: "Kira is truthful!" And Gosha said: "Two of us are lying." It turned out that three of them are lying. So who is telling the truth? Explain your answer.

In one class, all the girls are either blondes and beauties, or only beauties. And all the boys are either blondes and sportsmen, or only sportsmen. In total there are 14 boys and 13 girls in the class, and there are 18 blondes (boys and girls together). There is one more girl who is only a beauty than there are boys who are only sportsmen. How many beautiful blondes are there in the class?

From a board of 7 x 7 cells you need to cut out 9 rectangles of 1 x 3 cells each, so that afterwards no further such rectangle can be cut out. Give an example of how this can be done. Show your answer on the picture.

Ira thought of two two-digit numbers. The larger number ends with the same digit that the smaller number begins with. The difference between the larger and the smaller number is 43. Which numbers did Ira think of? Find all the possible answers.

Two tortoises, Borya and Gosha, set off at the same time along a straight track towards the finish. After a few minutes Gosha had run 6 metres and Borya had already run 8 metres. After another 4 minutes Borya finished, while Gosha still had 6 metres left to the finish. Gosha and Borya each ran at their own constant speed. What distance did they have to run? How many metres per minute did Gosha run?

In one class the children were solving a difficult addition sum. Half of the boys and ten girls got the wrong answer - each of them was wrong by 1 or by 2. All the rest got the correct answer. The answer "15" was obtained by thirteen people, "17" also by thirteen, "18" by two, and "19" by four. There were no other answers. How many girls are there in the class?

Sonya wrote the numbers from 50 to 100 on the board. Milana subtracted 22 from each number and also wrote the results on the board. Agafya added 66 to each of Milana's numbers and wrote those on the same board. How many numbers are written exactly once?

Beata performs the following operation on any triple of numbers: in place of each number she writes the difference of the other two (subtracting the smaller from the larger), and if the other two are equal she writes 0. For example, the triple (5, 2, 14) becomes (14 - 2, 14 - 5, 5 - 2), that is (12, 9, 3), and at the second step it becomes (9 - 3, 12 - 3, 12 - 9), that is (6, 9, 3). What triple of numbers is obtained after 2026 steps starting from the triple (5, 2, 1)?

Lyosha and Zoya are training for long-distance running. They start at the same time from the same place on a circular track and run at constant speeds (each at their own) in the same direction. Lyosha runs faster: after 45 minutes he had completed a full lap, turned round, ran towards Zoya and met her 15 minutes later. How long will it take Zoya to run a full lap?

Show how the figure in the picture can be cut along the grid lines so that 3 figures with the same perimeter are obtained. (The perimeter is the length of the boundary of a figure.) Show your answer on the picture.

14 monkeys are sitting in a circle facing the centre, each holding some fruit in its paws - a pear, an orange or an apple. On the command "Pass", each one passes its fruit to its neighbour on the right. The monkeys were given the command "Pass" twice. What is the largest number of monkeys that could have held a pear, an orange and an apple in their paws? Give an example confirming your answer, and explain why the number obtained really is the largest.

A crow with a large piece of cheese settled in a fir tree. Foxes, cats and mice came and began to praise the crow, hoping that she would treat them to some. At the end of each minute of praise the crow handed out rewards: to everyone who praised her with a "5" the crow threw 3 pieces of cheese, to those who gave a "4" - 2 pieces, and to those who gave a "3" she threw a fir cone and gave no cheese. In the first minute all the foxes gave "5", all the cats gave "4", and all the mice gave "3", and the crow handed out 23 pieces of cheese. In the second minute all the cats gave "5", all the mice gave "4", and all the foxes gave "3", and the crow handed out 24 pieces of cheese. In the third minute all the mice gave "5", all the foxes gave "4", and all the cats gave "3", and the crow handed out 28 pieces of cheese. How many fir cones did she throw altogether during this time?

Five wise men were led into a dark room and a black or white cap was put on each of their heads. After that the light in the room was switched on and they were told that the number of black caps is even. Will each of the wise men be able to work out which cap he is wearing, if he can see only the colours of the other wise men's caps?

Today 20 travellers gathered in the club. 10 of them had travelled in Europe, only 4 had not travelled in Asia, 6 travellers had made a tour of Africa, and 5 of America. None of them had made any journey in Australia. Each one had been on exactly two journeys in different parts of the world, and only Vasya had been to Antarctica alone. How many other travellers were in Antarctica together with Vasya?

Evklidikus drew a square on squared paper along the grid lines, with its vertices at grid nodes. It turned out that four rectangles with sides 3 and 4 fit inside it without overlapping, but four squares with side 4 do not fit without overlapping. What is the largest number of 2 x 2 squares that will definitely fit inside it? Show an example on the grid in the picture.

In Novosibirsk the time is always 4 hours ahead of Moscow. At 3:15 Moscow time, the electronic clock with a 24-hour display at the Novosibirsk railway station broke and began to run backwards at its previous speed. What will the time be in Moscow when the Novosibirsk clock shows 15:03 for the first time after the breakdown?

The medals for the Winter Games are kept in a safe with four combination locks. The Snow Leopard wants to think up four codes for them: one three-digit code and three two-digit codes. Each digit must occur no more than once, and each digit of the three-digit code must be equal to the sum of the digits of one of the two-digit codes. Will he be able to do this?

Merlin gave his pupil a card with a number on it in which each digit occurs once, and asked him to cross out 5 digits so that the remaining number would be as large as possible. The pupil got the number 97568, but if he had done everything correctly he would have got a number 564 greater. What is the smallest number that could have been on Merlin's card?
Two grey triangles were stuck onto a white rectangle of area 16 sq. cm, as shown in the picture. The area of the dark part (the overlap) is 5 sq. cm. What is the area of the white part?

topic: Arithmetic word problem – finding the whole or part
prob: The children got their hands dirty with black paint. Each child left two handprints on a sheet of paper. How many children were there altogether?
Sasha has 3 pencils of different colours and lengths. The red one is not longer than the others, and the blue one is shorter than the green one. Which pencil is the longest?
A rope was first folded in half, and then cut with scissors in three places, and the cuts were not made at the ends. How many pieces of rope were there?

One of the three brothers shown in the picture is called Petya. Work out which one, if it is known that two of them are liars and only one tells the truth. Write down the number shown under the picture of the boy as your answer. (Boy 1 says "I am Petya", boy 2 says "I am Petya", and boy 3 says "He is Petya", pointing at boy 2.)
Sasha has identical cubes and identical pyramids. 2 cubes together weigh 3 kg, and 4 cubes and 2 pyramids together weigh 10 kg (see the picture). How many kilograms does one pyramid weigh?

Mum cut a watermelon into several pieces and told Petya to share the pieces equally between two plates. One piece was left over, and Petya ate it. And then it suddenly turned out that the pieces had to be shared not between two plates but between three. Petya shared the pieces equally between three plates, and now he had two pieces left over. Petya ate those as well. Into how many pieces did Mum cut the watermelon, if Petya ate more pieces than there were on each plate?

An artist drew square portraits of the queen and the king. The portrait of the queen (without its frame) is 10 metres high, and the portrait of the king is 6 metres high. The width of the frame of the queen's portrait is 1 metre. How wide must the frame of the king's portrait be so that the portraits with their frames are the same height?

Little Vova jumps when he sees a cat, and claps when he sees a dog. However, today Vova made a mistake once and jumped at the sight of a dog instead of clapping, and once clapped at the sight of a cat instead of jumping. How many cats did Vova see today, if he clapped three times and there were eight animals altogether?

There are several figures. Choose exactly three different figures from them so that a 3 x 3 square can be made from them. The figures may be rotated and turned over, but they must not be placed on top of one another. Write down the numbers of the chosen figures from left to right in order as your answer.

There was a draughtsman (counter) in every cell of a square board. First Masha removed all the counters from the top row and the left column. Then Pasha came and removed all the counters from the bottom row. 6 counters were left on the board. How many counters were on the board at the start?

A rectangle of 6 x 4 cells is to be tiled with identical small figures. Figures with which number will NOT be suitable for this? Note: to "tile" means to cover with such figures without overlaps and without gaps. (The figures are: 1. a single cell; 2. a 1 x 2 domino; 3. an L-shaped tromino; 4. a 2 x 2 square; 5. a 5-cell P-shape; 6. a 2 x 3 rectangle.)

Kolya "counts" on a calculator by these rules:
A) If the number ends in 4, he adds 9.
B) If the number ends in 0, 2, 6 or 8, he adds 3.
C) If the number ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9, he subtracts 5.
Kolya started "counting" from the number 10. What number will he get after the seventh operation?

Masha drew 18 animals in a row - dogs, cats and mice. There are 5 cats altogether. After every cat there sits a mouse. There are twice as many mice as cats. After every dog there sits a cat. How many dogs are there in Masha's drawing?

How many different line segments can be found in the picture? For example, AD and AE are two different segments. (The labelled points are A, B, C, D, E and F, using the Russian letters A, B, V, G, D, E in the diagram.)

Sharik weighs as much as three Matroskins, and together Sharik and Matroskin weigh as much as Uncle Fyodor. But even if you put all three of them together, they will only make up half the weight of Pechkin. Pechkin weighs 80 kg. How much does Matroskin weigh?

5 workers had nails, and 4 workers had screws. Some of them could have had both nails and screws. Then the worker Uncle Kolya arrived with nails and screws, and the number of workers with both nails and screws became 3. How many workers are there now altogether?
There are 6 cards: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Using all the cards, make the smallest number in which neighbouring digits differ either by 3 or by 2.

9 people stood in a circle - knights and liars. Knights always tell the truth, and liars lie in every sentence. Each person said: "The next 2 people to my right are liars." How many knights are there among them?

Several cats came to a meeting from the yard, the same number of cats from the park, and fewer - 3 cats - from the car park. After that they divided into 3 equal groups and went off to catch mice. How many cats were there altogether, if there were fewer than 20 of them?

topic: Arithmetic word problem – finding the whole or part
prob: Tolya has one sweet. Sasha has 10 times more and one more. Valya has 10 times more than Sasha, and one more. Kostya has 10 times more than Valya, and one more. How many sweets do the children have altogether?
A dice was thrown 7 times. The total sum of the points that came up was 10. What is the largest number of points that could have come up in one of the throws?

Masha was writing down the numbers in order - 1, 2, 3 and so on. At some point she got bored, wrote the last number, and noticed that she had written the digit 1 fifteen times, the digit 2 fifteen times, and the digit 3 fourteen times. What was the last number she wrote?

Kostya bought two rulers, three exercise books and four pencils for 69 roubles. Olya bought five rulers, six exercise books and seven pencils for 144 roubles. By how many roubles is a ruler more expensive than a pencil?

Yana had a pencil case, and in it an odd number of pens. On the first day she added one pen to the pencil case, on the second day 2, on the third day three, and so on. On the eighth day she added 8 pens and noticed that the number of pens in the pencil case had become several times greater than it was at the start. What is the largest number of pens Yana could have had in her pencil case at the start?

You have 4 cards with the words "One", "Two", "Three" and "Four". You need to arrange them in a row so that neighbouring cards have no letters in common. Give an example of how this can be done. Write your answer using the corresponding digits. (The words are the Russian ODIN, DVA, TRI, CHETYRE.)

There are cubes in four boxes. In any two boxes the number of cubes is different, and there are no empty boxes. In the first and second together there are 3 cubes. In the third and fourth together there are 10 cubes. In the second and fourth together there are 4 cubes. How many cubes are in the third box?
The figure in the picture is made up of six identical rectangles. The perimeter of the figure is 54 cm. What is the length of the longer side of a rectangle?

Pooh and Piglet pick apples at a constant speed - each at their own. One day they decided to fill a large basket. Pooh started picking earlier than Piglet. By one o'clock in the afternoon 5 apples had been picked, by two o'clock 15, and by three o'clock 25. At four o'clock Pooh and Piglet finished picking and there were 39 apples in the basket. How many apples did Piglet pick?

Masha drew a picture on the wall just like the one shown. Masha also has three paints. She colours in the circles on the picture. Circles joined by a line segment must not be coloured the same colour. How many different colourings of the picture can she get?

Five people were sitting in a queue at the clinic waiting for the doctor. Among them were Igor Nikolaevich, Pavel Arkadyevich (second from the end of the queue) and Anfisa Mikhailovna (second from the start of the queue). For 15 minutes none of them went in to see the doctor, but two more people arrived and joined the queue, and Igor Nikolaevich had to leave for work, so he went away. Now Pavel Arkadyevich was third from the start of the queue, and Anfisa Mikhailovna was fifth from the end. What position from the start of the queue was Igor Nikolaevich in?

topic: Arithmetic word problem – finding the whole or part
prob: Innokenty Afanasyevich bought a square marble slab with a side of 2 metres and cut it into small squares with a side of 20 cm. With these small squares he tiled the floor of a porch measuring 1 metre by 60 centimetres at his dacha, and from all the ones left over he made a path one small square wide from the porch to the well. How far is the well from the porch of the dacha? Give the answer in metres.

Every 19 steps he takes, Vitya stumbles. And Rita sneezes every 15 steps. One day in the street Vitya and Rita saw each other at the same moment and walked towards each other at the same speed. By the moment they met, Vitya had managed to stumble 3 times and Rita had sneezed 5 times. What was the distance in steps between Vitya and Rita when they noticed each other?

Sveta doubled each digit of some three-digit number, rearranged the resulting three digits in some way, and added the resulting three-digit number to the original one. She got 516. What is the original number? (Numbers do not begin with the digit 0.)
Katya has two red, one green and seven blue beads. How many different necklaces can she make using all ten beads, if there must be exactly one red bead next to the green bead?

A teacher wrote ten whole numbers in a circle on the board. He asked the pupils in the class to add to each number the next one clockwise. Then to do the same thing again with the new circle. And finally to add up all the numbers in the resulting circle. Masha got a sum equal to 284, Kolya 283, Andrey 282, Roma 278, and Ira 274. One of the pupils got the correct answer. Which one?

In the Magic City there live 15 kind inhabitants and 100 greedy ones. When a Magic Fruit (or part of one) reaches a kind inhabitant, he divides it into three parts. One he eats himself, and the other two he gives to two people who have not yet eaten any Magic Fruit today. A greedy one, on receiving a Magic Fruit, immediately eats the whole thing himself. Today one Magic Fruit grew in the garden of each of seven inhabitants of the Magic City. What is the largest number of inhabitants who could have eaten Magic Fruit today?

Knights, liars and squires are standing in a circle - 15 people in all. Knights always tell the truth, liars always lie, and squires tell the truth only to knights. Each of them said to their neighbour on the right: "To the left of me is a liar!" What is the largest number of liars there could have been in the circle?

Find four different two-digit numbers beginning with the digit 2, such that the sum of any two of them is divisible by their difference, and such that the difference between the largest and the smallest number is greater than 7. Write down the sum of these four numbers as your answer.
Two little sticks have got lost from the apartment number (see the picture). What is the apartment number?

In the yard there lived puppies, kittens and lambs. Their names are: Chub, Tom, Chudo, Luchik, Tuchka, Pirat, Bim and Richi. The kittens' names have one letter fewer than the puppies' names. If an animal is black, then its name contains the letter "Ch", and if it is a different colour, then it does not. What is the name of the ginger puppy? (The names are the Russian CHUB, TOM, CHUDO, LUCHIK, TUCHKA, PIRAT, BIM, RICHI.)

topic: Arithmetic word problem – finding the whole or part
prob: Baubles of three kinds were hanging on the Christmas tree: red, gold, and striped red-and-gold. The baubles must be put into two boxes, where red baubles may go only in the red box and gold ones only in the gold box. Petya put all the striped baubles with the red ones, and got 11 baubles in the red box and 7 in the gold box. Masha moved all the striped baubles over to the gold ones. Now there are 6 baubles in the red box and 12 in the gold box. How many baubles of each kind were hanging on the tree?
Petya took a square sheet of paper and folded it in half twice, as you see in the picture. Then he cut three shapes out of the folded sheet. How many holes will Petya find when he unfolds the sheet?

There are 6 fruits in a vase: apples, pears and bananas. Anya, Vanya, Masha and Grisha counted the fruits in the vase, but sometimes miscounted by 1. The results of their counts are given in the table. Study them and answer the questions. A) How many fruits of each kind were there? B) Who made the fewest mistakes? C) Who was wrong all three times? (Counts - Anya: apples 3, pears 1, bananas 4. Vanya: 2, 2, 2. Masha: 1, 2, 2. Grisha: 2, 1, 2.)

Masha and her younger brother Petya found two boxes with the same number of sweets under the tree at New Year. Starting from 1 January, Petya ate one sweet from his present every day. Masha ate one sweet and moved a second one into her beloved brother's box. On Sunday Masha had her last two sweets left; she ate one and moved the other to her brother, and her sweets ran out. On 18 January Petya ate his last sweet. On what date was the Sunday when Masha ate her last sweet?

All the Roman numerals on a clock face are made up either of straight identical sticks (|) or of slanted ones (/, \), which are also identical. Anya is colouring the numerals on a paper clock face. Anya colours one straight stick in 1 minute, and one slanted stick in 1 minute 30 seconds. Today Anya coloured in some three numbers that come one after another on the clock face, and spent exactly 10 minutes. Which numbers did Anya colour? Find all the possible answers.

10 fir trees grow around a clearing at equal distances from each other. A hare and a wolf run round the circle from tree to tree in one direction (shown by the arrow in the picture). It is known that while the hare runs from tree No. 7 to tree No. 2, the wolf runs the whole circle. The hare started at tree No. 8 and then ran to tree No. 9 and on round the circle. The wolf also ran round the circle and caught up with the hare at the fourth tree. At which tree was the wolf when the hare was at the eighth tree?

Misha drew a square, and Tanya drew another square on the same sheet. Then Misha painted over both squares with paint, and an octagon (eight-sided figure) was formed. Draw in the space on the right how this could have happened.

On Monday 10 February, Egor truthfully said: "I will tell the truth only on Monday or Thursday, if the date on that day is an even number, and on the other days I will lie." On what date will he first be able to tell the truth again? (Even numbers are numbers that can be split into two equal parts, for example 2, 4, 6, ...; the others are odd.)

11 children are standing in a circle. Petya threw the ball round the circle to the right, over one person, to Olya. Olya also threw the ball to the right over one person, and the children carried on throwing the ball in the same way. Gena received the ball only after the tenth throw. What is Gena's number, if Petya is counted as the first and all the places are numbered in the direction the ball travels?

The numbers 3, 4, 2, 1 are written in a row. In one move you are allowed to swap any two numbers (not necessarily neighbouring) whose sum is odd. How can you put all the numbers in order in 3 moves? (Even numbers are numbers that can be split into two equal parts, for example 2, 4, 6, ...; the others are odd.)

The children, arriving at the buffet, started counting their money. Gena says: "I have 20 roubles." Ivan says: "I have 15 roubles less than Gena." Petya says: "Together you have exactly enough money for one pie." Lena said: "A pie costs 35 roubles." Gena added: "Oh yes, I have 25 roubles." It is known that four of the statements are correct and one is wrong. How much money does Ivan have?
Vova has one red cube, one green cube and 3 blue cubes. In how many ways can Vova build a tower of 3 cubes?

18 people were gathering a harvest - some gathered only the tops, some only the roots, and some gathered both. If you add together the number of those who gathered tops and those who gathered roots, you get 27 people. There were 7 more people gathering tops than those gathering roots. How many people gathered only the tops?

In a family there are more than three children of different ages. Each of the children was one year old or more, and the sum of their ages is 11 years. A year later the sum of the ages of the children in the family became 15 years, and one more year later 20 years. How many children are there now in the family, and how old is each child?
Yana, Eva and Milana have 10 pencils altogether, and Yana has the most. Two pencils got lost, and now Yana has the fewest. How many pencils did Milana have?

Along a straight road stand the little houses of Krosh, Nyusha, Losyash, Pin and Yozhik - in exactly that order. Krosh and Yozhik like visiting their friends, but always return home in the evening. On Monday Krosh visited Nyusha, and Yozhik visited Losyash. On Tuesday Krosh visited Losyash, and Yozhik visited Pin. On Wednesday Krosh went to Pin, and Yozhik went to Nyusha. On these days Krosh and Yozhik went nowhere else. It turned out that over these three days Yozhik walked 17 kilometres and Krosh walked 19 kilometres. What is the distance from Krosh's house to Yozhik's house?

A large square was made up of identical small squares. The number of small squares that have exactly 4 neighbouring squares (neighbours are those sharing a common side) is 25. How many small squares have exactly 3 neighbours?

Masha has 3 times as many pencils as pens in her pencil case. She lost one pen but added 3 pencils. After this there were 4 times as many pencils as pens. How many pens were in the pencil case at the start?

Vasya and Petya are riding bicycles in opposite directions round a circular track. The length of the track is 900 metres. They ride at constant speeds: Vasya at his own speed, Petya at his. Vasya rides a full circle in 3 minutes, and meets Petya once every 100 seconds. One day, after one of their meetings, they set off in the same direction with the same speeds. How long after this meeting will Vasya draw level with Petya for the first time?

Ira has 2-rouble and 5-rouble coins in her money box. Oleg also has 2-rouble and 5-rouble coins, but he has as many 2-rouble coins as Ira has 5-rouble coins, and as many 5-rouble coins as Ira has 2-rouble coins. Oleg's total amount is twice as much as Ira's. Ira has three 5-rouble coins. How many 5-rouble coins does Oleg have?

Can the numbers 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 7, 8 be placed in the circles (see the picture) so that the sums of the numbers along the sides of the triangle are each equal to 16? If the answer is "yes, it can", give an example on the picture. If the answer is "no, it cannot", explain why.

The number 9876543210 is written on a sheet of paper. Anfisa wants to divide it with commas into several numbers so that, for any two neighbouring numbers, the right-hand one is greater than the left-hand one. What is the largest number of commas Anfisa can place?

The central cell was removed from a 5 x 5 board. Cut the remaining part of the board along the grid lines into identical four-cell figures so that each of them contains exactly one circle. Note: the figures may be rotated and turned over. They must be the same in shape, not only in the number of cells. Show your answer on the picture on the right.

A careless confectioner packs sweets into boxes standing in a row in front of him. First he puts one sweet into the first box. At each next step he puts into the next box as many new sweets as there already are in all the previous boxes taken together, and then moves one sweet from every non-empty box into it. How many sweets in total will be arranged in the boxes when the fourth box becomes empty?

At a holiday centre there are gazebos along a path. Their total number is less than 11. Each gazebo has the same number of people resting in it. In all the gazebos on the left of the path there are, in total, 13 more people resting than in the gazebos on the right of the path. What is the largest number of people that can be resting at the holiday centre in all the gazebos altogether?

In a town there are 4 streets running from south to north, and 5 streets running from west to east (see the picture; the distances between neighbouring streets may be different). Every day the mayor of the town goes for walks at the same speed. His walk along the first route took him 64 minutes, along the second 68, and along the third 16. How many minutes will the mayor need to walk along the fourth route?

A certain two-digit number with no zeros in it is shown on a computer screen. Alina added 23 to it and divided the result in half. Igor took the number obtained by swapping the digits of the number on the screen, and multiplied it by 3. Alina and Igor got one and the same result. What number is written on the screen?
A square made of several small cells was drawn on paper. Ink was accidentally splashed onto it. Work out how many cells of the square the ink landed on.

Olya and Yulya live in the same stairwell. Olya lives on the second floor and Yulya on the tenth. One day the girls set off at the same time from their flats and walked towards each other at the same speed. On which floor will they meet?

Lena, Kolya, Lev and Katya went to the forest. Those whose name begins with "K" had a basket, and those whose name begins with "L" had a small hamper. The boys gathered mushrooms, and the girls gathered berries. What was the name of the person who brought back the basket of berries? (The names are the Russian LENA, KOLYA, LEV, KATYA.)
Tolya had 2 short sticks and several long ones. Tolya broke each long stick into three parts, and they became short. Now Tolya has 11 sticks. How many sticks were there at the start?
Yesterday Lena suggested to Ira: "Let's go to the cinema the day after tomorrow!" Today is Friday. On which day of the week did the girls plan to go to the cinema?

topic: Arithmetic word problem – finding the whole or part
prob: There were 7 pies on the birthday person's table. Each guest ate half a pie, and the birthday person ate a whole pie. After this no pies were left on the table. How many guests were at the party?

Determine the weight of the weight marked with a question mark, if in both cases the scales are balanced. (In the picture: on the first scales, a 10 kg weight and a cat balance a crow and a 14 kg weight; on the second scales, a 10 kg weight and a crow balance a cat and the unknown weight.)

There is a rectangular sheet of paper. One side is grey, and the other is squared (marked with a grid). It was folded as shown in the picture. At the bottom a white square appeared, made up of 4 cells. How many cells does the whole sheet consist of?

First-grader Vasya visited six theatres in his town, and first-grader Dima visited nine. It turned out that among any four theatres there is one that both of them visited. How many theatres are there in the town altogether?

Winnie-the-Pooh and Piglet had the same number of chestnuts in their bowls. Winnie loves chestnuts, but Piglet does not. Winnie-the-Pooh quietly ate half of the chestnuts from Piglet's bowl. And then Piglet moved half of what was left in his bowl into Winnie-the-Pooh's bowl. Now Winnie has 15 chestnuts in his bowl. How many does Piglet have?

Next week the king ordered everyone to rest from Thursday to Sunday (inclusive). The queen ordered everyone to rest on Monday, and then every other day. On which day of the week will the townspeople manage to work?
Ground squirrels lived in five burrows. In each there was a different number, and more than one squirrel. There were 21 squirrels in all. The most squirrels lived in the biggest burrow. How many?

There were 32 sweets in a box. Malysh took some of the sweets into his pocket, and Karlsson put the rest into his two pockets. Then Karlsson begged and ate 2 sweets from Malysh. After this it turned out that each of the three pockets had an equal number of sweets. How many sweets did Malysh manage to take for himself at the start?

Liars always lie, and knights are always truthful. One day five liars and one knight got together. The first says: "I am not a liar." The second: "That is true." The third: "There are no liars here." The fourth: "Among us there is exactly one knight." The fifth: "No, we are all knights." The sixth: "I've got a bit confused." Which of them is the knight?

Lena gathered carrots, beetroot, tomatoes and aubergines in the garden. There were equal numbers of carrots and beetroot, the number of tomatoes was the same as the number of carrots and beetroot together, and there were more aubergines than carrots, beetroot and tomatoes together. Lena brought back 12 vegetables in all. How many aubergines did she bring?
Myumziks are bigger than shibziks but smaller than zyamziks. And two krakozyabras are the same as one myumzik. Which of them is the biggest?

Along a road there are a House (H), a Pharmacy (P), a Bank (B), a Shop (S) and a Fitness centre (F) - see the picture. Ilya drove from the House to the Shop, 5 km, then to the Pharmacy, 4 km, then set off for Fitness, 6 km, and dropped in at the Bank, 3 km. What is the distance from the Shop to the Bank? (The order along the road is H, P, B, S, F.)

Petya tossed 10 coins: 3 coins of 5 roubles each, and the rest of 2 roubles each. When they landed, Petya added up the numbers on the coins that fell tails up - the total was 11. How many coins landed heads up?
Sveta has 9 squared tiles - see the picture. She put together a large square from all the tiles except one (with no overlaps and no gaps). Which tile was left over (give its number)?

Three hares and two cats weigh the same as two hares and three cats. A hare and a cat together weigh 10 kg. All the hares weigh the same and all the cats weigh the same. How many kilograms does a cat weigh?

topic: Arithmetic word problem – finding the whole or part
prob: Milana and Sveta have 30 watermelons together. Milana lost 5 watermelons and gave 2 away to a girl called Olya. Sveta was given 9 more, and after this Sveta and Milana had an equal number of watermelons. How many watermelons did Sveta have at the start?

Andrey was colouring the cells in his exercise book. The first was blue, then green, then red, then blue, then green, then red, and so on. The last one was green. Between the second green and the last green there are 8 cells. How many cells are there between the first red and the last blue?

Eva has 9 mushrooms in her basket - ceps and saffron milk-caps, with more ceps. Yana has 13 mushrooms - ceps and chanterelles, with more chanterelles. It turned out that Yana has more ceps than Eva. How many ceps does Eva have?

Marina bought 7 bananas and put them into 3 bags. There were no empty bags, and the different bags had different numbers of bananas. On the first bag she wrote: "there are fewer bananas here than in each of the other bags", on the second: "there are more bananas here than in each of the other bags", on the third: "the first and second bags together have fewer than six bananas". Marina is not very good at counting, so all the labels turned out to be wrong. How many bananas are in the second bag?
Lena thought of a two-digit number and then subtracted half of it. The resulting number has a digit sum of 6 and a digit product of 5. What number did Lena think of?

A square table with a side of 3 metres stands in a rectangular room. The distance from the table to one wall is 7 metres, and to another wall is 5 metres. The sum of the lengths of the short and long sides of the room is 21 metres. What is the sum of the distances from the table to the two other walls?

Katya wrote a three-digit number on the board and went off about her business. Amir came along, rubbed out the first digit, and added a 5 at the end. Then Lyosha came to that same number, which had appeared after Amir, rubbed out the first digit, and wrote a 4 at the end. Katya came back and noticed no changes - the number was the same as the one she had written. What number did Katya write?

Kristina came to school before everyone else and wrote a two-digit number smaller than 30 on the board in the classroom. Nikita, Misha, Slava and Vitya looked into the classroom and told their classmates what the number was. Nikita said it is divisible by 12. Misha said it is divisible by 3. Slava said it is divisible by 2. Vitya said the number is 24. It is known that only two people told the truth. What number is written on the board?

12 people studied in the 2nd class. Each studied English or Chinese: 7 children studied English, 9 Chinese. The summer passed, and the children moved up to the 3rd class. The English group decreased by 4 people, and the Chinese group by 6. What is the largest number of children who can study both languages in the 3rd class?

Along a highway are the villages A, B, C, D in exactly that order. It is known that from B to D is 10 km. From A to C is 8 km. From B to C is the same distance as from C to D. How far is it from A to B? (The villages are the Russian A, B, V, G.)

Ten people stand in a circle: five in red overalls, the rest in blue. Each of them has a bucket - with red paint or with water, and there are no more buckets of paint than of water. On command, each person poured the contents of their bucket over their neighbour on the right. It turned out that after this the overalls of all ten people became red. How many buckets of paint were there?
The sum of two two-digit numbers is equal to AAA, and their difference is equal to AA, where A is a certain digit. Find the smaller of these two-digit numbers.

Three riders - the Baron, the Viscount and the Count - rode across a bridge. The Baron said afterwards that he overtook the Count right at the end of the bridge, and did not meet the Viscount at all. The Viscount reported that he met the Count riding towards him in the middle of the bridge. Which of the three was the last to leave the bridge?
There are five children of different ages in a room. The middle one is 7 years old. The three youngest together are older than the two oldest. By how many years is the oldest older than the youngest?

Arkady lives on the seventh floor of a thirteen-storey building, and his friend lives in the same stairwell but lower down. One day Arkady left his flat and took the lift to visit his friend. However the lift was broken: first it took Arkady down to the first floor, then up to the top floor, and only after that did it go down to the required floor. In the end Arkady's journey took 9 times longer than if the lift had been working properly. On which floor does Arkady's friend live?

The class lined up in a row. The teacher asked three of the pupils how many people there were to the left and to the right of each of them. He wrote down the six numbers obtained in a random order, and moreover wrote one of the numbers down wrongly by accident. This is what he got: 3, 5, 9, 14, 19, 21. How many pupils are there in the class?

Martians come in three types: with three, with five or with nine antennae. One day 100 Martians gathered in a spacious hall, and there were twice as many Martians with three antennae as Martians with nine antennae. How many antennae were there in the hall altogether at that moment?

The chess piece Purposeful King moves, like an ordinary King, by one cell, but only forwards, to the right, or forwards-right along the diagonal. The Purposeful King began its journey from the bottom-left corner of an 8 x 8 chessboard and reached the top-right corner in exactly 11 moves. How many moves to the right did it make?

A two-digit number n begins with the digit 2. All the numbers from 1 to n can be divided into 4 groups so that each group has the same number of numbers, and the sum of the numbers in each group is also the same. Find n.

Kai and Gerda each threw three snowballs at snowmen and scored the same number of points. Hitting the bottom ball of a snowman is 1 point, hitting the middle ball is 2 points, hitting the head is 3 points, and hitting the bucket on the head is 4 points. All three of Kai's hits are marked on the left snowman. Two of Gerda's hits are marked on the right one. Mark Gerda's third hit on the picture.
Buratino had 12 more gold coins than Basilio. Buratino bought five crusts of bread, and Basilio bought two. Now they have an equal number of coins. How much does a crust of bread cost?

A grasshopper can jump from any circle with a number on it to a neighbouring one (see the picture). It jumped three times in one direction, then turned back and jumped another 11 times in the other direction. The grasshopper ended up on the circle with the number 7. From which circles could it have started?

Numbers - twos and ones - are written in all the cells of a square. It is known that the sum of the numbers in the cells shaded in the first picture is 3, in the second 5, and in the third 6. What is the sum of all the numbers in the square?

In Liza's family there are 5 women (counting Liza). In the picture they are shown as circles. Among them are Liza's great-grandmother and her sister. Each line joins a mother and a daughter. Colour in the circles that could represent Liza. Note: a great-grandmother is the grandmother's mother. Show your answer on the picture.

Pechkin was carrying a parcel from the post station to Prostokvashino. He rode his bicycle at one and the same speed. The whole journey of 18 km took him 60 minutes. When he had ridden half the way, he started singing songs. Pechkin stopped singing when he had 3 km left to ride to Prostokvashino. For how many minutes did Pechkin sing?

Two gnomes put diamonds into their sacks. The first said: "If you take half the diamonds from your sack and add another 9 diamonds, you will get the same number of diamonds as I have." The second said: "And if you take half the diamonds from your sack and add another 3, you will get the same number of diamonds as I have." How many diamonds were in each one's sack?

Three square ski tracks were laid out in a park: a small one 4 km long, a medium one 8 km long, and a large one 13 km long. Vasya went one lap along the thick (bold) line. How many kilometres did Vasya walk?

A queen can capture the opponent's pieces along a file (vertically), along a rank (horizontally), and along a diagonal. Mark all the cells from which the queen can capture all three pawns at once. Show your answer on the picture.

Arina is standing on the first step of a long staircase and makes "moves". The first "move" is 3 steps up, the second "move" is 1 step down. Then 5 up, 2 down, 7 up, 3 down, and so on. On which step will Arina be after making 10 of her "moves", if the pattern continues?

On an island there are only knights (who tell only the truth) and liars (who tell only lies). Three islanders met one day - Anton, Borya and Vasya. It is known that among them there are one or more liars. Anton says to the others: "You two are knights." Borya replies: "Vasya is a knight." Who is who?

A Hare, a Wolf, a Fox and a Squirrel each drew a different straight line (one each), and marked several points on them. On the Hare's and the Wolf's lines there were 3 points each, and on the Fox's and the Squirrel's there were 5 points each. Altogether there turned out to be 10 points. How could this be? Draw a suitable picture in the space on the right.

Tolya has four cardboard circles of different colours (blue, red, yellow, green) and four squares of different colours (the same ones). Tolya wants to take one circle and put it on one square, or the other way round - take one square and put it on one circle. In how many ways can he do this, if a red figure may not be placed on a red one?

A teacher wrote the seven digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 in a row in some order, with 7 turning out to be second from the right. The second-graders named several two-digit numbers that they saw on the board: 62, 13, 56 and 35. In what order are the digits written on the board?
Misha swims 2 pools in 2 minutes, Kolya is twice as slow, and their dad is twice as fast as Misha. Dad swam 15 pools more than Kolya in the same time. In what time?

Sasha has 5 cards with one number on them and another 5 cards with a different number. From the numbers on three cards Sasha can make a sum of 9, and from the numbers on four cards he can make a sum of 8. What two numbers could be on Sasha's cards? Find all the possible answers.
Sonya and Masha are 13 years old together now. In 12 years' time Sonya will be 4 times as old as she is now. How old is Masha now?

Kostya and Ellina spent five days preparing for the olympiad. Both made little calendars and numbered the days of preparation from 1 to 5. If on some day Kostya solved a lot of problems, he called that day good, and if not - bad. Ellina named her days in just the same way, according to her own progress. Kostya turned out to have 2 bad days, and the sum of the numbers of these days is 6. Ellina's bad days were the first day and two other days. If the numbers of her bad days are multiplied together, the result is a number divisible by 10. Kostya and Ellina had exactly one good day in common. Which days turned out to be good for Kostya?

After a heavy snowfall Yana went out to clear the yard of snow. At one o'clock in the afternoon, when she had already removed 400 kg of snow, Olya and Tolya came to help her; they clear snow at the same speed as Yana. When there were 200 kg of snow left to clear, the others said to her "You carry on by yourself" and left. Yana finished clearing the snow at 4 o'clock in the afternoon. In what time would Yana have cleared all the snow working on her own?

Olya has 20 apples arranged in 5 piles. In one move you may move any number of apples from one pile to another. Tolya says that, no matter how the apples are arranged, in one, two or three moves you can make the number of apples equal in all five piles. Yana claims that this is not so. Who is right - Tolya or Yana? Why?

Kristina thought of two digits and wrote out all the two-digit numbers made up of these digits. For example, if she thought of 5 and 1, then she wrote out the numbers 55, 11, 51 and 15. Then she added the resulting numbers together. The sum turned out to be 374. What is the smallest number Kristina wrote out?

Along a road, a hundred birch trees were planted one metre apart and numbered in order - first, second, and so on. Just then five sparrows landed on five of them. Then the sparrows began to fly from birch to birch by the following rule: if some sparrow flies from one birch to another, then some other sparrow immediately flies the same number of metres, but in the opposite direction. At a certain moment all the sparrows ended up on the 10th birch. What is the largest number the birch could have had, on which the 4th sparrow (by distance from the first birch) was sitting at the start?

Arkady sawed a log into 8 small logs. Arkady's dad sawed each small log into several billets (different small logs could be sawn into different numbers of billets). Altogether there were 30 billets. How many saw-cuts did dad make in total?

Arkady carefully shuffled nine cards numbered from 1 to 9 and dealt three cards each to his dad, his mum and himself. All three of the numbers on Arkady's cards turned out to be less than 5. Dad's, on the contrary, were all greater than 5. Exactly two of mum's numbers are divisible by 3. Which numbers did Arkady get?

Arkady and his dad found a treasure - 20 one-rouble coins - and began to divide it. Arkady tosses the coins one at a time. If it lands heads, he puts that coin into his own pocket. If it lands tails, dad takes for himself both that coin and three more coins not yet played for (or all of them, if fewer than three are left). In total Arkady tossed 7 coins. How many coins did Arkady end up with?

On the Far Island live knights and liars. Knights tell only the truth, and liars always lie. One day five islanders met on a clearing: Au, Bu, Vu, Gu and Du. Au said: "Among us five there are more liars than knights!" Bu declared: "Vu is a knight!" Vu replied: "Bu is a knight!" Who among them are knights, if Gu and Du are liars?

A Martian has 3 or 4 arms. On Mount Olympus (the highest peak on Mars) and in the Hellas valley (the deepest lowland on Mars) live equal numbers of Martians. The first group have 53 arms in total, and the second 67. How many Martians live on Mount Olympus?

Princess Jasmine arranged a hundred gems into six caskets, putting at least one in each. In the first, second, fourth and sixth caskets there were 64 gems in total. In the third there were 34 more gems than in the first. In the sixth there were more than in the fifth, and 25 times fewer than in the fourth. How many gems are in the second casket?

A hundred gnomes in shirts with the numbers 00, 01, 02, ..., 98, 99 gathered to hold a tournament in the game of gnomeball. The hardest thing for gnomes is always dividing into teams. In each team there is one goalkeeper and equal numbers of right-wing and left-wing players. The teams must have equal numbers of players, and moreover no two gnomes agree to play in the same team on the same wing if the numbers on their shirts begin with the same digit or end with the same digit. Will the gnomes manage to divide into teams under these conditions? If so, into how many teams?
A refrigerator is filled with food as shown in the picture. How many glasses of juice can be placed on the shelf of the refrigerator so that the juice does not spill? The food may not be moved.

Mum of 3 children bought a poppy-seed bagel and a crusty baguette for breakfast. Mum needs to divide the bagel and the baguette equally among all her children, giving each one an equal piece of each. How many cuts in total will Mum need to make? The bagel and baguette cannot be cut together with one cut.
A group of hares and squirrels invited three piglets to their party. There were more hares than squirrels, but fewer than the piglets. How many participants were there at the party in total?

One day a mouse found a square slice of processed cheese on the table. "Good cheese should have holes!" thought the mouse. She folded it in half twice and gnawed out holes, as shown in the picture. How many holes will there be in the slice of cheese if it is now unfolded?

Masha said: "I am 6 years old." Liza said: "I am 1 year older than Masha." Katya said: "I am the same age as Masha." Mum knows that one of the girls told an untruth, and that together the girls are 10 years old. How old is the girl who told the untruth?

Two famous spies from class 1 'A', Masha and Kolya, encoded their names with a made-up cipher (in the first rectangle), and also the place of their meeting (in the second). Identical letters are identical symbols, and different letters are different symbols. Name the place where they plan to meet.
Vasya Petrov's birthday this year fell on a Thursday. On what day of the week was the birthday of his friend Petya Vasechkin, if he is 12 days older than Vasya?

Petya had these little parts: 7 "corners" (L-shaped three-cell pieces) and 10 "sticks" (1x3 three-cell pieces). He put together squares, like the one in the picture (a 4x4 square), for as long as he had enough of the parts he needed. What is the smallest number of parts that could be left over? The parts may be turned over.

Winnie-the-Pooh was tidying up his store cupboard. There he found 5 identical pots exactly half filled with honey, weighing 5 kg each. "This won't do," thought Winnie. And he moved the honey into two pots, which came out full, and ate the extra honey. It turned out that the two full pots and the honey in them weigh 16 kg. How much honey does Winnie now have in his store?

Pavlik has 13 cubes of three different sizes: small ones with a side of 2 cm, medium ones with a side of 3 cm, and large ones with a side of 4 cm. Pavlik built 3 towers: one from all the large cubes, one from all the medium cubes, and one from all the small cubes. All the towers turned out to be the same height. How many medium cubes did Pavlik have?
The fox Alice stole from the wealthy Buratino the same number of coins as Basilio, plus another 4 coins - 9 coins in all. How many coins were stolen from Buratino by Alice and Basilio together?

Four pirates grabbed weapons: a dirk, a pistol, a club and a sabre, each their own. Ahmet did not grab the pistol. Captain Botik took the dirk. The club was not given to John or Galya. The sabre was also taken away from Galya. What was left for Galya?

In a castle there are 11 doors and they are all closed. When someone passes through a door, a closed door becomes open, and an open one closes. The queen, the princess and the king in turn walked from the castle entrance to their chambers. How many doors ended up open? (See the plan of the castle in the picture.)
One Puzan weighs the same as five Karapuzes, and a Karapuz the same as two Malyavkas. One Malyavka weighs 5 kg and another half a Malyavka. How many kilograms does a Puzan weigh?

Vintik glued a tunnel together from his cubes, which looks the same from behind as from the front. Shpuntik built a tower from all his cubes, but did not glue the cubes together, stacking them one on another. How many cubes does Shpuntik need to add so that he can glue together the same tunnel as Vintik's? (The tunnel and the tower are shown in the picture on the right.)

The cat Vasily managed to steal a third of the sausages from a packet and shared them with Barsik and Murzik, who also took part in the operation. Each got his own third of the loot, and Vasily got 2 sausages. How many sausages were there in the packet?

In each grey cell Losyash put one digit so that the sum of any three cells in a row is 11 and no two identical digits stand next to each other. What is the sum of all the numbers in the cells? (One cell already shows a 4; see the picture.)

Anya has 4 dried rings (bagels) and 8 matches. She made the largest number from all these objects, with a total digit sum of 14. What is this number? Note: Anya can only make these digits: 0 - from one ring, 8 - from two rings, 1 - from two matches, 4 - from four matches.

The alien Gosha (G) can step to a cell that shares a side with the one where he is standing. Each step Gosha changes his colour: red to blue to yellow to red and so on. Right now he is red, and he wants to reach the cell Ship (S) so as to be blue when he arrives there. How many steps will he have to make? Note: you may not step onto a cell twice. The thick lines are walls and you may not pass through them. Find all the variants (you do not need to prove there are no others).

On a 3 x 3 board Sasha placed a white bishop and a black king so that they do not attack each other. In how many different ways can Sasha do this? Note: a king attacks all neighbouring cells, and a bishop attacks all cells along the diagonals. Sasha does not rotate the board.

topic: Arithmetic word problem – finding the whole or part
prob: Kristina had 27 sweets, and Marina had fewer. Kristina gave 10 sweets to Marina, and then the girls had an equal number of sweets. How many sweets did Marina have at the start?

Octopuses and hares came to visit the director of the zoo - 11 animals in all. The director's doorbell was not working, so each one, on arriving, knocked at the door. An octopus knocked 8 times, once with each leg, and a hare 4 times, once with each paw. Altogether the director counted 64 knocks. How many octopuses came to visit the director?

The very strong girls Katya, Lena, Anya and Ellina are carrying a long log. One girl carries one end of the log, another the other end, and the remaining two carry it in between. The distance from Lena to Katya is 5 metres. From Ellina to Katya it is 3 metres, and to Lena it is less. From Anya to Ellina it is 5 metres, and to Katya it is less. What is the length of the log in metres?

One day 10 squirrels, several hares and several foxes got together and decided to hold a masquerade. The hares dressed up as squirrels, the foxes as hares, and the squirrels - some as hares, some as foxes. It came out as 4 squirrels, 6 hares and 7 foxes. How many foxes were there at the start?

At a summer camp the children were split into three teams of several (2 or more) people - teams "A", "B" and "C". A draughts tournament was held among the children - everyone played everyone else exactly once. Between the children of team A and team B, 35 games were played, and between the children of team A and team C, 77 games. How many children are in team B?

Several children decided to buy a large watermelon, paying equally - 100 roubles each. However after some time three more children joined them, and now, to buy the very same watermelon, each has to pay 70 roubles. How many children were there at the start?

Five apples, four pears and 3 oranges weigh 1 kilogram 160 grams together. Seven apples, 5 pears and 3 oranges weigh 1 kilogram 420 grams together. How much do an apple, an orange and a pear weigh together?

Marina, Kristina and Lena gathered 9 strawberries. The strawberries had these weights: one each of 1, 3 and 10 grams, and two each of 2, 6 and 12 grams. The girls divided the berries so that the total weight was the same for each. Kristina got two berries. What do you get if the weight of the first berry is multiplied by the weight of the second?

Tolya's jacket has a great many pockets. One day he began putting little screws into the pockets. In the first pocket he put one screw, in the second 2, in the third 3, and so on, until he had filled all the pockets. Observant Kristina said: "You could have arranged all these screws with 9 in each pocket, and all the pockets would also have been filled." How many pockets does Tolya have?

On two opposite faces of a small cube the letter A is written, on two other opposite faces also the letter A, and on the remaining two opposite faces the letter B. From 27 such cubes a large cube was glued together and given to Tolya. What is the largest number of letters B, in different places on the cube, that Tolya could count by turning the cube in his hands?
Arrange the numbers from 1 to 10 in a row so that the sum of any two neighbouring numbers ends in a 5 or a 6.

Grandmother baked 35 cabbage pies and 42 jam pies and shared them out among her grandchildren. So that none of the grandchildren would be upset, each of them got the same number of cabbage pies, and also the same number of jam pies. How many grandchildren could grandmother have had, if there is more than one? Note: the pies may not be broken up when sharing - they would spoil before their time!

Arkady and Boris were gathering mushrooms in the forest, and they came across exclusively saffron milk-caps and russulas. Each of them gathered 45 mushrooms, and the number of Arkady's saffron milk-caps turned out to equal the number of Boris's russulas. If each of them had gathered twice as many saffron milk-caps, then Arkady would have had 13 mushrooms more than Boris. How many russulas are in Arkady's basket?

Arkady drew a 5 by 5 cell square on squared paper and coloured some 10 cells of his square red. After that he counted how many red cells he had in each horizontal row, how many red cells in each vertical column, and how many red cells on each of the two diagonals of the square. The sum of the twelve numbers obtained turned out to be 25. It is known that the central cell of the square is red. How many red cells in total lie on the diagonals of the square?

25 sweets are arranged in 10 boxes so that each box has no more than three sweets. There are no empty boxes. It is known that there are at least four boxes with 2 sweets each. How many boxes have one sweet in them?

Several boys and girls were playing in the yard, and there were seven more boys than girls. Sasha was taken home for lunch, and now there were four times as many boys as girls. Is Sasha a boy or a girl, and how many boys were playing in the yard after Sasha went home?

Aliens, as everyone knows, come in red and blue. One day ten aliens put on hats and began to dance in a round dance. Exactly at midday every alien holding hands with aliens of a different colour ate their own hat. What is the largest number of hats that could have been eaten?
The cell figure shown in the picture is called a "flag". What is the smallest number of "flags" you need to take so that a square of some size can be made from them?

The boy Vitya set off on a scooter from point A and rode, without changing speed, along a circular route whose plan is shown in the picture. It is known that from point A to point G he rode for 10 minutes. From point B to point V it took 3 minutes. From B to D, 12 minutes. From E to A, 17 minutes. How many minutes did he ride from point Zh to point Z? (The labelled points on the route are A, B, V, G, D, E, Zh, Z.)

Several posts stood in a yard. The residents of the yard decided to stretch a rope between every two posts, to dry washing on these ropes. How many posts are there in the yard, if the number of ropes turned out to be ten times greater than the number of posts?

Masha has only balls and bows for decorating Christmas trees. Each little tree already has a ball and a bow. Add more decorations to each little tree so that these conditions hold: there are no more than 7 decorations on each tree; all the trees have different numbers of decorations; and for each tree the following is true: if you add one ball to it, it will have equal numbers of bows and balls. Show your answer on the picture.

Three identical candles stood on a table in a room. Each burns down in two hours. A gnome first lit the first candle. When it had burned halfway down, he lit the second one. When the second candle had burned halfway down, he lit the third one. The third candle burned to the end. For how long in total was the room lit by the candles?

topic: Arithmetic word problem – finding the whole or part
prob: Hedgehog cut all his apples into parts and began to treat his friends. Three little squirrels got a quarter of an apple each, and two little hares got a half each. A big bear cub ate a whole apple. The last quarter of an apple Hedgehog ate himself. By how many more does Hedgehog have friends than apples?

A path 1 metre wide was made from a little house to a well, as shown in the picture. The length of the outer edge, marked with a dotted line, is 20 metres. Find the length of the inner edge, marked with a solid line.
Petya was making figures out of hexagonal parts, increasing their size. How many parts does he need for the next figure?

Some of these boxes contain sweets, and the rest of the boxes are empty. On the empty boxes the labels are false, and on the boxes with sweets the labels are true. Circle the boxes that contain sweets. (The four box labels read: "All these boxes are empty"; "At least one of these boxes is not empty"; "All the boxes except this one are empty"; "At least one of these boxes is empty".) Show your answer on the picture.

For the New Year Anya made up this puzzle: K + R + O + L + I + K = K + O + T (identical letters are identical digits, and different letters are different digits). What is the smallest digit that can correspond to the letter T? Give an example for the smallest digit T. (In Russian, KROLIK means 'rabbit' and KOT means 'cat'.)
Igor sees in a mirror the reflection of a digital clock - 21:51. What time is it really?
Place 6 crosses so that in each column, in each row and in each marked figure there is exactly one cross. Show your answer on the picture.

Three piglets found an unknown animal in the forest. Nif-Nif said: "It is a cat or a mole." Nuf-Nuf said: "It is a mole or a raccoon." Naf-Naf said: "It is not a mole, and not a raccoon, and not a cat!" Only one of them is mistaken. What animal did they find?

In a box there are 6 different dominoes. How are they arranged? Note: each domino consists of two little squares, on each of which a number from 0 to 6 is written. (The 4x3 grid of numbers reads, row by row: 5 5 2 2 / 0 0 3 5 / 5 3 5 0.)

At the river there were 16 boys, and each was either wet, or sunburnt, or both. There were 2 more wet boys than sunburnt ones, and 6 boys were wet and sunburnt at the same time. How many sunburnt dry boys were there at the river?

In how many ways can 6 children be divided into 3 pairs to play chess, if Masha does not want to play with Kolya? Note: the order of the children in a pair does not matter (the pair Pasha and Lyuda is the same as the pair Lyuda and Pasha). The order of the pairs also does not matter.

From 10 cards 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 0 three numbers were made, each greater than 0, and they were added together. In the answer there turned out to be five digit '9's. Could this happen? Note: if "no", explain why; if "yes", give an example of how to do it.

The yacht "Beda" was delayed in port and fell behind in the race. "Beda" will reach the point where the yacht "Black Cuttlefish" now is in 3 hours. "Black Cuttlefish" now has 6 hours left to the finish. "Beda" is 3 times faster than "Black Cuttlefish". Who will reach the finish earlier, and by how many hours?
